# UX Audit Roll-up — demo app

**Verdict: GO.** Usability and accessibility each found one minor issue and nothing
blocking. The cuj auditor ran static and therefore verified nothing — it is reported as
`Unscored`, never folded in as a pass, which is the shape the suite scorecard could not
represent while `pct` was a mean of its members.

## Per-auditor results

| Auditor | Mode | P0 | P1 | P2 | P3 | Total | Health | Result |
|---------|------|----|----|----|----|-------|--------|--------|
| usability | live | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 1 | 90% Excellent | one minor issue |
| accessibility | live | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 1 | 92% Excellent | one minor issue |
| cuj | static | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | — Unscored | nothing verified |

## Auditors that ran vs. skipped

Three auditors ran. Web performance was skipped: opt-in, not requested. The cuj auditor
ran but could not verify anything in static mode, so it is `Unscored` rather than scored
`0` or `100` — both of those would be false, in opposite directions.

## Merged top issues

1. **[P2 · usability]** [Promo-code error is vague](usability-20260715-143000.md#p2-promo-code-error-is-vague) — the message states no reason.
2. **[P2 · accessibility]** [Promo-code input has no programmatic label](accessibility-20260716-090000.md#p2-promo-code-input-has-no-programmatic-label) — the field is optional, so a workaround exists.

## Verdict rationale

No `P0` and no `P1` anywhere in the suite, so the gate opens. The unscored cuj run does not
change that: it found nothing because it verified nothing, and the roll-up says so rather
than counting it as a clean pass.
